title: SGLT2 inhibitor-induced genitourinary infections and the consequent antimicrobial-antidiabetic drug interactions: A narrative review of clinical and pharmacovigilance concern.
what: Sodium glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular and renal benefits in type 2 diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and heart failure, but their use is associated with genitourinary (GU) infections and medication-safety concerns during antimicrobial treatment. This narrative review integrate evidence regarding SGLT2 inhibitor-associated GU infections, antimicrobial-antidiabetic drug interactions, pharmacovigilance, clinical management, and antimicrobial stewardship.
source: PubMed, Diabetes research and clinical practice
original_title: SGLT2 inhibitor-induced genitourinary infections and the consequent antimicrobial-antidiabetic drug interactions: A narrative review of clinical and pharmacovigilance concern.

title: Model-informed precision dosing of vancomycin and amikacin in critically ill neonates: a pre- and post-intervention study.
what: Optimal antimicrobial dosing in neonates is complicated by extreme developmental pharmacokinetic (PK) variability. Traditional therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) fails to achieve PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) target attainment in this vulnerable population.
original_title: Model-informed precision dosing of vancomycin and amikacin in critically ill neonates: a pre- and post-intervention study.
